sections.title: No article before a job
sections.content: To say what you do for a living, just put the profession right after vagyok, with no article in front of it: Tanár vagyok ("I'm a teacher"), not Egy tanár vagyok. This is different from English, which always needs "a/an" before a job. In the third person, van drops out the same way it does with any noun predicate you already know: Károly mérnök ("Károly is an engineer"), not Károly van mérnök.

items.english: I'm a teacher, at a school in Budapest.
Zsófia is a doctor, and Tamás is a cook.

sections.content: Egy tanár vagyok isn't just extra — it actually sounds odd in Hungarian, more like "I am some teacher" than a simple statement of your job. Drop the egy whenever a profession follows vagyok, van, or vagy directly.
